card: Documents in libbitcoinkernel headers that the btck_WriteBytes callback may pass a null pointer when the byte count is zero. Today the header leaves this behavior unspecified, even though internal vector-backed implementations pass through std::vector::data() which returns null for empty script and witness items. Clarifying this interface contract primarily prevents undefined behavior and crashes in strict foreign language bindings.
evidence: Commit message notes that 'empty elements are ordinary script data' and 'This matters for bindings rather than for C callers.'
problem: The header does not specify whether the buffer pointer can be null when size is zero. Writers backed by standard containers pass through std::vector::data(), which can return null for empty witness stack items and script elements, potentially triggering invalid assumptions or undefined behavior in language bindings.

risk.why: It only updates header comments documenting existing libbitcoinkernel callback behavior without altering executable code.

scope_notes: Small documentation-only update to a libbitcoinkernel header.
summary: Document in the libbitcoinkernel C API headers that the bytes pointer passed to btck_WriteBytes can be null when size is zero. It clarifies the callback contract for callers implementing custom writers.
